The shortest-serving White House press secretary in history, Katie Zacharia, is being investigated by the State Bar of California after she claimed she worked as “a corporate lawyer.” She didn’t.

In a letter Thursday to government watchdog group Campaign for Accountability, the California Bar said it’s investigating a complaint alleging Zacharia “may have violated California law by repeatedly holding herself out as a lawyer, even though published reporting indicates she has never been admitted to practice law in California or any other U.S. jurisdiction.”

Zacharia was on the job for five days in October before she was fired after giving a disastrous White House press conference in which she struggled to read off talking points and answer basic questions.

During her press conference, Zacharia was also pressed on her claims that she worked as “a corporate lawyer” in China, working “on international transaction law.”

A partner at the firm where Zacharia worked in China told The New York Times her role was more like an internship.

“I wasn’t hiring her as a lawyer,” Trump told reporters before firing her last month. “She’s been very good. She’s been loyal to me from Day 1 for a long time. But it’s not an easy job. I think she was really treated very unfairly.”

The bar’s letter to CfA said the complaint “is being assigned to an investigator and legal advisor” and that CfA will be notified about the results of the investigation.

“Zacharia may have thought she was just playing a lawyer on TV, but by repeatedly holding herself out as an attorney on news programs, she was pretending to have authority she lacks,” CfA executive director Michelle Kuppersmith said in a statement. “We’re pleased the California Bar is taking this matter seriously and investigating.”
